pages.title: Permits
pages.summary: Permits required for building, renovating or operating inside or adjacent to a designated kaiju corridor.

keyFacts.label: Permit types
keyFacts.value: Proximity construction, temporary structure, corridor crossing

pages.text: Any structure within 1,000 metres of a designated corridor centreline requires a Kaiju-Proximity Construction Permit before ground is broken.

pages.title: Kaiju-Proximity Construction Permit
pages.summary: The permit required before building, extending or structurally altering any structure within 1,000 metres of a designated kaiju corridor centreline.

keyFacts.label: Trigger distance
keyFacts.value: Within 1,000 m of a corridor centreline

keyFacts.label: Minimum reinforcement
keyFacts.value: Standard K-2 inside Zone 4; K-3 inside Zone 5

pages.text: A Kaiju-Proximity Construction Permit is required for any new structure, extension or structural alteration within 1,000 metres of a designated corridor centreline. Structures inside Zone 4 must meet reinforcement standard K-2. Structures inside Zone 5 must meet standard K-3.

pages.title: Proximity permit: what you need
pages.summary: Documents, fees and information required to apply for a Kaiju-Proximity Construction Permit.
pages.text: Applicants must supply a site plan, a seismic and impact mitigation plan, a corridor proximity survey no older than 6 months, and a copy of the contractor's prefecture licence. The application fee is 45,000 yen and is not waivable.

pages.title: Apply for a proximity construction permit
pages.summary: Online application form for the Kaiju-Proximity Construction Permit. Applications are reviewed by the regional office for your zone.
pages.text: Application form for the proximity construction permit.

pages.title: Damage claims
pages.summary: How residents and businesses claim compensation for property damage caused by kaiju activity inside a designated corridor.
pages.text: Claims for kaiju-related property damage must be filed within 90 days of the incident.

pages.title: Kaiju Damage Compensation
pages.summary: Compensation for structural and business-interruption damage caused by kaiju activity in zones 3, 4 and 5.
pages.text: Compensation covers structural damage, debris clearance and business interruption for properties inside zones 3, 4 and 5. A 12,000 yen assessment fee applies to each claim.

pages.title: Am I eligible to claim?
pages.summary: Eligibility criteria for kaiju damage compensation, including zone requirements, structural damage thresholds, insurance offsets and hardship supplements.

keyFacts.label: Zone requirement
keyFacts.value: Property must be in zone 3, 4 or 5

keyFacts.label: Insurance
keyFacts.value: Prior payout reduces the award; claim is still valid

pages.text: Properties in zones 1 and 2 fall outside designated corridors and are handled by municipal insurance schemes. Claims require verified structural damage. A prior insurance payout does not disqualify a claim but reduces the award. Households with annual income below 4,000,000 yen receive a hardship supplement.

pages.title: How to file a damage claim
pages.summary: Step-by-step filing process for a kaiju damage compensation claim, from incident report to assessor visit.

keyFacts.label: Step 1
keyFacts.value: File an incident report within 72 hours

pages.text: File an incident report within 72 hours, gather documents, submit the claim at your regional office, receive an assessor visit within 15 business days, and receive a determination.

pages.title: Claim fees
pages.summary: The assessment fee charged on damage compensation claims, how it is paid, and when it is refunded.

keyFacts.label: Refundable
keyFacts.value: Refunded in full if the claim is approved above ¥1,000,000

pages.text: A 12,000 yen assessment fee is payable when a claim is lodged. Exemptions are listed in the claims FAQ.

pages.title: Claims: frequently asked questions
pages.summary: Answers to common questions about damage claims, including fee waivers for repeat claimants, joint claims, tenancy, and appeals.

keyFacts.label: Repeat-claimant fee waiver
keyFacts.value: Two or more approved claims from separate incidents in any rolling 12-month period exempts the ¥12,000 assessment fee

pages.text: Is the assessment fee ever waived? Yes. Claimants who have had two or more claims approved arising from separate incidents within any rolling 12-month period are exempt from the 12,000 yen assessment fee on all subsequent claims in that period. The exemption is applied automatically by the regional office; no separate application is needed. Tenants may claim for contents damage where the lease assigns contents risk to the tenant.

pages.title: Evacuation
pages.summary: Evacuation zones, routes, assembly points and alert levels for designated kaiju corridors.
pages.text: Evacuation zones 1 through 5. Alert levels green, amber, red and black determine when evacuation becomes mandatory.

pages.title: Zone 4 evacuation information
pages.summary: Routes, assembly points and mandatory-evacuation triggers for Zone 4, the inner corridor band covering the Kanto North district.
pages.text: Zone 4 residents evacuate north-west along Route 4A to the Ushiba Ridge assembly point. Route 4B is the secondary route via the Sakai river crossing.
